claim: About 20 years ago, researchers studying ovarian cancer discovered that many cases of high-grade serous ovarian cancer, the most common type, originate in the fallopian tubes.
label: TRUE
annotatorNote: [AI label: Claude, 2026-10-13 - not yet checked by the human annotator] CURE (3 Mar 2011): Dana-Farber researchers, starting in 2005, found early serous cancers in the fallopian tubes, which 'are likely the origin of many high-grade serous ovarian tumors'. Ovarian Cancer Research Alliance (undated grantee page, 2023 grant): 'The most common and most lethal type of ovarian cancer is high grade serous carcinoma (HGSC)'; 'the majority of "ovarian" HGSCs originate from the fallopian tube epithelium'. 2005 is about 20 years before. The 2006 pathology papers were not read: PubMed refused this session.
